## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root. `enrichVolcano` (the
user's own package, not on CRAN) is called with `::` for its label cleaner.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readr, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/06_set_association/a_script/06_set_association.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Four inputs: the set catalogue from `00_build_gene_sets`, the singscore matrix from
`04_run_singscore` (one row per set, one column per sample), the sample targets stored with the
protein estimates and the per-leg phenotype measurements. The singscore matrix travels as rds,
not through a workbook, because a round trip through xlsx breaks the exact rank ties the tests
below depend on. Reading `proteins.rds` loads limma, which defines its stored class, and R says
so in the output.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "06_set_association")
set_catalog <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "set_catalog"
)
set_score <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "04_run_singscore", "c_data", "set_scores.rds"))
targets <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))$targets
phenotype <- read_csv(here("00_Input", "phenotype.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(set_score)
head(targets[c("sample_id", "participant", "leg", "treatment", "timepoint")], 6)
```

## Select sets

Only sets the catalogue marks as `qualifies` are tested. `values` holds their scores in catalogue
order, and `collection_sizes` counts sets per collection; that count is the denominator for the
chance comparison further down.

```{r select-sets}
catalog <- set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, database, pathway, measured_size)
values <- set_score[catalog$set_id, ]
collection_sizes <- count(catalog, database)
collection_sizes
```

## Pair the samples

Every comparison here is paired, so each sample needs its partner. `by_timepoint` spreads the
targets to one row per leg, with the T1 and T2 sample IDs side by side. `legs` keeps legs sampled
at both time points. Treatment comes from the targets, never the leg letter: leg assignment was
counterbalanced.

```{r pair-legs}
by_timepoint <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  select(leg_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sample_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = sample_id)
legs <- drop_na(by_timepoint, T1, T2) |> arrange(participant, treatment)
head(legs, 4)
```

`pair_by_treatment()` takes a leg table and the name of the column that identifies each leg, and
returns one row per participant holding both legs, BFR and HLRT, in that column. Participants
missing either leg are dropped.

```{r pair-participants}
pair_by_treatment <- function(data, column) {
  data |>
    select(participant, treatment, value = all_of(column)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = value) |>
    drop_na(BFR, HLRT)
}
delta_pairs <- pair_by_treatment(legs, "leg_id")
c(legs = nrow(legs), change = nrow(delta_pairs))
```

The change in each set's score per leg is T2 minus T1. Its columns are named by leg, so the BFR
and HLRT legs of a participant can be picked out with `delta_pairs`.

```{r change-scores}
delta <- values[, legs$T2] - values[, legs$T1]
colnames(delta) <- legs$leg_id
```

## Prepare the phenotype

Four outcomes, each a post minus pre change in one leg: cross-sectional area (`csa`) and echo
intensity (`echo`) of vastus lateralis (`vl`) and rectus femoris (`rf`). Echo intensity falls as
muscle composition improves, so a negative change is the favourable one. The join is declared
one-to-one, because a duplicated phenotype row would silently misalign every leg below.

```{r leg-phenotype}
outcomes <- c("vl_csa", "vl_echo", "rf_csa", "rf_echo")
leg_phenotype <- legs |>
  left_join(
    select(phenotype, -treatment),
    by = c("participant", "leg"), relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vl_csa = vl_csa_post_cm2 - vl_csa_pre_cm2,
    vl_echo = vl_echo_post_au - vl_echo_pre_au,
    rf_csa = rf_csa_post_cm2 - rf_csa_pre_cm2,
    rf_echo = rf_echo_post_au - rf_echo_pre_au
  )
head(select(leg_phenotype, leg_id, treatment, all_of(outcomes)), 4)
```

The differential analysis works within participant: BFR minus HLRT for the score change and for
each outcome change. Participant traits that move both legs cancel out of that difference.

```{r paired-differences}
paired <- delta[, delta_pairs$BFR] - delta[, delta_pairs$HLRT]
colnames(paired) <- delta_pairs$participant
paired_outcome <- map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
  value <- set_names(leg_phenotype[[name]], leg_phenotype$leg_id)
  value[delta_pairs$BFR] - value[delta_pairs$HLRT]
})
```

## Correlate each set

Spearman correlation ranks both variables and correlates the ranks, so it measures any monotone
relationship and is not pulled by single extreme legs. `spearman_by_row()` takes a matrix of
score changes (sets in rows) and one outcome vector, and returns one row per set with the number
of observations, Spearman's r and its p-value.

`cor.test()` gives the exact Spearman p at these sample sizes; the t approximation is off by up to
9e-4. Tied values make it warn and fall back to the approximation, so those warnings are
suppressed.

```{r spearman}
spearman_by_row <- function(values, outcome) {
  fits <- suppressWarnings(apply(values, 1, function(row) {
    test <- cor.test(row, outcome, method = "spearman")
    c(r = unname(test$estimate), p = test$p.value)
  }))
  tibble(
    set_id = rownames(values), n = sum(!is.na(outcome)),
    r = unname(fits["r", ]), p = unname(fits["p", ])
  )
}
```

Two analyses per outcome. Pooled correlates every leg's score change with its outcome change,
both arms together. Differential correlates the within-participant differences. BH adjustment
runs within each analysis, outcome and collection, never pooled across them.

```{r set-association}
set_association <- map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
  bind_rows(
    pooled = spearman_by_row(delta, leg_phenotype[[name]]),
    differential = spearman_by_row(paired, paired_outcome[[name]]),
    .id = "analysis"
  ) |>
    mutate(outcome = name)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(analysis, outcome) |>
  left_join(select(catalog, set_id, database, pathway), by = "set_id") |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, "BH"), .by = c(analysis, outcome, database))
head(arrange(set_association, p), 6)
```

The same correlation inside each arm, for description only: it feeds the figure insets and the
`set_by_arm` sheet, and nothing is tested on it.

```{r by-arm}
by_arm <- map(set_names(c("BFR", "HLRT")), function(treatment) {
  keep <- leg_phenotype$treatment == treatment
  map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
    spearman_by_row(delta[, keep], leg_phenotype[[name]][keep]) |>
      mutate(outcome = name)
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "treatment")
```

## Check results

One row per analysis and outcome: every set tested once, the number of observations, the range of
r and any missing p-value.

```{r check}
set_association |>
  summarise(
    sets = n(), observations = first(n), r_min = min(r), r_max = max(r),
    missing_p = sum(is.na(p)), .by = c(analysis, outcome)
  )
```

## Compare with chance

With thousands of sets, some reach p < 0.05 by luck alone. The chance expectation is 5% of the sets
tested: the number of nominal hits a collection returns when no set truly tracks the outcome. The
ratio of observed nominal hits to that count reads 1 at chance. Each collection gets its own
denominator, so a 41-set collection is not read against a 1,366-set one, and BH runs inside the
same split for the same reason.

```{r chance}
chance_expectation <- set_association |>
  transmute(
    analysis = paste0("association: ", analysis), comparison = outcome, database,
    n_pairs = n, p, fdr
  ) |>
  summarise(
    features = n(), nominal = sum(p < 0.05), expected = round(n() * 0.05, 1),
    ratio = round(nominal / expected, 2), fdr_sig = sum(fdr < 0.05),
    .by = c(analysis, comparison, database, n_pairs)
  )
head(chance_expectation, 6)
```

## Draw figures

The figure helpers below are shared line for line with `05_set_classification`. `figure_theme` is
the common look. `caption_text()` takes a figure title, the caption text and the page position,
and returns the wrapped caption. `paginate()` takes rows with a `panel` factor and a function that
draws one page, and returns a list of plots, twelve panels to a page. It builds each page from
that page's rows, because a paginating facet would build every panel for every page.
`chance_page()` draws the chance ratios as bars. `write_pdf()` writes a list of plots to one A4
PDF in `b_reports/`.

```{r figure-helpers}
figure_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 6.8, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(3, 3, 4, 3)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(4, "mm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    legend.position = "top"
  )
caption_text <- function(title, text, page = 1, n_pages = 1) {
  pages <- if (n_pages > 1) sprintf(" (page %d of %d)", page, n_pages) else ""
  str_wrap(sprintf("%s%s. %s", title, pages, text), 115)
}
paginate <- function(data, draw, title, text, scales = "fixed") {
  pages <- split(data, (as.integer(data$panel) - 1) %/% 12)
  imap(unname(pages), function(page, i) {
    draw(droplevels(page)) +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3, nrow = 4, scales = scales) +
      labs(caption = caption_text(title, text, i, length(pages))) +
      figure_theme
  })
}
chance_page <- function(data, y, facet, title, text) {
  ggplot(data, aes(ratio, .data[[y]], fill = ratio > 1)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_col(width = 0.65) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%d of %d", nominal, features)),
      hjust = -0.12, size = 2.5, colour = "grey25"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[facet]]), ncol = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "grey72"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
    labs(
      x = "observed nominal hits / chance expectation", y = NULL,
      caption = caption_text(title, text)
    ) +
    figure_theme +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
write_pdf <- function(pages, name) {
  pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", name), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
  walk(pages, print)
  invisible(dev.off())
}
```

`chance_line()` takes a collection and returns the caption sentence giving its chance count.
`set_label()` turns a collection and pathway name into a wrapped panel title.

```{r label-helpers}
chance_line <- function(db) {
  n <- collection_sizes$n[collection_sizes$database == db]
  sprintf("Nominal p, uncorrected: chance alone returns %.1f of the %d %s sets.", n * 0.05, n, db)
}
set_label <- function(database, pathway) {
  str_wrap(paste0(database, ": ", enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000)), 40)
}
```

`association_figure()` takes an analysis, its S-number, a title, a description of the population
and a collection, and returns scatter pages for every set and outcome pair in that collection
reaching nominal p, smallest p first, or an empty list when there are none. Each panel plots
every leg's score change against its outcome change, with a line fitted inside each arm and the
within-arm correlations inset.

```{r association-figure}
association_figure <- function(which_analysis, number, title, population, db) {
  hits <- set_association |>
    filter(analysis == which_analysis, database == db, p < 0.05) |>
    arrange(p)
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  points <- pmap(hits, function(set_id, database, pathway, outcome, r, p, fdr, ...) {
    arms <- by_arm |>
      filter(set_id == !!set_id, outcome == !!outcome) |>
      mutate(text = sprintf("%-5s n=%d  r=%+.2f  p=%.3f", treatment, n, r, p))
    tibble(
      panel = sprintf(
        "%s\nvs %s   r = %+.2f   p %s   q %s",
        set_label(database, pathway), outcome, r, signif(p, 2), signif(fdr, 2)
      ),
      change = delta[set_id, ], d_outcome = leg_phenotype[[outcome]],
      treatment = leg_phenotype$treatment, caption = paste(arms$text, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)))
  paginate(points, function(page) {
    ggplot(page, aes(change, d_outcome, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_text(
        data = distinct(page, panel, caption), inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = caption), family = "mono",
        hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.25, size = 1.9, lineheight = 1.2, colour = "grey25"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.35))) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC"), aesthetics = c("colour", "fill"),
        name = NULL
      ) +
      labs(x = "change in set score, T2 - T1, one point per leg", y = "change in phenotype")
  }, sprintf("S%d Figure", number), paste(
    paste0(title, ", ", db, "."),
    sprintf(
      "All %d %s set-outcome pairs whose Spearman correlation reaches nominal p in the %s",
      nrow(hits), db, which_analysis
    ),
    sprintf("analysis (%s), smallest p first.", population),
    "Lines are fitted within each arm; the header r is the", which_analysis, "correlation and",
    "the inset gives it within each arm. q from BH within collection and outcome.", chance_line(db),
    "Data: set_association and set_by_arm sheets of 06_set_association.xlsx."
  ), scales = "free")
}
```

One PDF per collection, so each can be read on its own: S17 for the pooled analysis, S18 for the
differential one. S19 is the chance page across all analyses and outcomes.

```{r write-figures}
walk(unique(catalog$database), function(db) {
  write_pdf(
    c(
      association_figure(
        "pooled", 17, "Training response against phenotype, all legs",
        sprintf("%d legs, both arms pooled", nrow(legs)), db
      ),
      association_figure(
        "differential", 18, "BFR minus HLRT, within participant",
        sprintf("%d paired participants", nrow(delta_pairs)), db
      )
    ),
    paste0("06_association_", db, ".pdf")
  )
})
write_pdf(list(chance_page(
  mutate(chance_expectation, panel = paste0(sub("association: ", "", analysis), ", ", comparison)),
  "database", "panel", "S19 Figure", paste(
    "Nominal hits relative to chance, by collection. Spearman per set, uncorrected p. Bar length",
    "is observed nominal hits divided by the count that collection returns under the null; red",
    "clears 1, grey does not. Labels give observed of tested. Data: chance_expectation sheet of",
    "06_set_association.xlsx."
  )
)), "06_chance_by_collection.pdf")
```

## Summary

Nominal hits as a multiple of chance, by analysis, outcome and collection, then the sets
surviving BH in each analysis and outcome.

```{r summary}
chance_expectation |>
  select(analysis, comparison, database, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = database, values_from = ratio)
summarise(chance_expectation, fdr_sig = sum(fdr_sig), .by = c(analysis, comparison))
```

## Save results

`06_set_association.xlsx` opens with an `overview` sheet, then `chance_expectation` (nominal hits
against chance), `set_association` (r, p and BH q per set, analysis and outcome, smallest p
first), `set_by_arm` (the within-arm correlations) and `set_catalog` (every tested set).

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  chance_expectation = chance_expectation,
  set_association = arrange(set_association, p),
  set_by_arm = by_arm,
  set_catalog = catalog
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "Nominal hits against chance, per collection. Read this first.",
    "Set against phenotype change: pooled, then within participant.",
    "The same correlation computed inside BFR and inside HLRT, descriptive.",
    "Every tested set with its collection and measured size."
  )
)
write_xlsx(
  c(list(overview = overview), sheets),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "06_set_association.xlsx")
)
```
